key_insight: Applying differential privacy in federated learning measurably degrades common explanation signals (feature attributions and model sparsity), but the paper quantifies that trade-off and offers practical mitigation strategies (e.g., privacy-aware feature selection and DP-budget tuning) to recover interpretability without sacrificing required privacy guarantees.
problem_solved: Clarifies how adding Differential Privacy (DP) to Federated Learning (FL) affects explainability (XAI) — quantifying loss of attribution fidelity, stability, and sparsity — and provides actionable guidance to balance privacy and interpretability.
method: Controlled empirical evaluation of FL models with DP (varying ε, clipping) across tasks, comparing XAI techniques (e.g., SHAP/LIME/feature importance).
Define and measure explainability metrics (attribution fidelity, stability/variance across clients, and feature sparsity) to quantify DP impact.
Propose and test mitigation strategies: privacy-aware feature selection, adaptive DP budget allocation, and model simplification to improve explanations under privacy constraints.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners concrete metrics and recipes to choose DP parameters and XAI tools in FL systems so they can meet privacy requirements while retaining usable explanations for debugging, compliance, and end-user trust.
visual_elements: Privacy vs Explainability trade-off curve: x-axis = DP strength (lower ε = more private), y-axis = explanation quality (e.g., attribution fidelity).
Schematic of federated system: client nodes → DP mechanism (noise, clipping) → central model, annotated where explanations are computed and degraded.
Bar/heatmap comparing XAI metrics (stability, sparsity, fidelity) across DP settings and XAI methods (SHAP, LIME, feature importance).
Checklist/flow diagram of mitigation steps: feature selection → DP-budget tuning → model simplification → re-evaluate explanations.
paper_title: Towards Explainable Federated Learning: Understanding the Impact of Differential Privacy
paper_authors: Júlio Oliveira, Rodrigo Ferreira, André Riker, Glaucio H. S. Carvalho, Eirini Eleni Tsilopoulou
